title: XRAY NT1 Set-Up Book
notes: 2.3MB official XRAY PDF, verified via pdftotext. Explicit 'Effects of X Adjustment' sections for every parameter plus a corner-section/throttle-position framework (entry/mid/exit). 1/10 nitro on-road. Diagrams image-only but all explanatory prose extracts cleanly. Top-tier KB source.

title: XRAY T1R Set-Up Book
notes: 1.1MB XRAY setup book verified via pdftotext. Genuine cause->effect prose (more negative camber = more grip; toe-in stabilizes at the cost of traction; link length -> roll center -> front/rear traction). 1/10 touring. Hosted on a French retailer mirror, but content is authentic XRAY material; URL resolves.

title: MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (Mugen Seiki Racing, by Adam Drake)
notes: 8-page manufacturer-hosted PDF (204KB), verified via pdftotext. Pure cause->effect for nearly every 1/8 nitro buggy parameter, framed on-power/off-power steering throughout. Closes with the 'one change at a time' rule. Some non-ASCII chars mojibake and need cleanup, but all text is recoverable. Among the best explaining-docs found.

title: 8IGHT Tuning Guide (Team Losi Racing, 800-0317v1.1)
notes: 11-page official TLR fixed PDF, verified via pdftotext. Each adjustment has a labeled definition plus explicit handling effect, framed around front-vs-rear balance. Full 1/8 nitro buggy. Includes a sample/blank sheet at the end, but pages 2-8 are dense tuning-effects prose. Top-tier extraction candidate.

title: R/C Handbook V2 (Scott Guyatt, off-road edition, hosted by Team Associated)
notes: Manufacturer-hosted e-book PDF (234KB), clean pdftotext extraction. Full off-road buggy setup theory with a glossary plus 'why' explanations for every system. Brand-agnostic theory, off-road focused. This is Associated's FREE handbook (distinct from their paid 'RC Cheat Sheets'). Same document also mirrored on petitrc as RC_HandbookV2.pdf; the V3-4 merged edition supersedes it.

title: R/C Handbook V3-4 (Scott Guyatt, merged off-road + on-road)
source: Scott Guyatt / Heavy's Hobby Shop, updated by Team Associated (hosted on petitrc.com)
notes: Canonical merged handbook: Guyatt's off-road buggy + touring booklets combined, brand-agnostic. ~129k chars — the largest single concept guide found. Glossary + per-setting cause->effect. Supersedes V2.

title: RC Cheat Sheets — Set Up Your Radio-Control Car to Win
notes: ~113-page one-concept-per-page A-Z effect encyclopedia, split on-road vs off-road plus electrical/nitro/pan. ~69k chars extract cleanly. Broadest concept coverage of any single file (2.1MB). NOTE: distinct from Team Associated's paid 'RC Cheat Sheets' product — this is a free community-hosted compilation.

title: Team Associated TC3 Tuning Guide
source: Michael Lufaso & Team Associated (hosted on petitrc.com)
notes: Classic 17-page touring tuning bible. Opens with weight-transfer/roll-pitch-yaw theory + driving style, then A-Z per-parameter 'what is it / how to change / what it does'. Author notes most tips apply to all cars. ~66k chars extract cleanly.

title: Team Associated RC10B4 Tuning Guide
notes: Per-setting B4 guide, 'what it is / when to change / what it does'. Image-heavy (~7MB) but text layer extracts (~15k chars). B4 wording, generic 2WD-buggy logic.

title: HUDY Set-Up Book (All-In-One Set-Up Solution)
notes: 1/10 touring reference: how to MEASURE and ADJUST every parameter in a defined set-up order, with rationale. ~97k chars via pdftotext (a plain web-fetch markdown converter fails on its compressed streams — use pdftotext). More procedure/measurement than pure handling-effect, but teaches the why of each step. RaceLab's existing KB already draws on HUDY.

title: Chassis Tuning 101 — Matt 'Murfdogg' Murphy's Dirt Oval Tuning Guide
notes: 21-page dirt-oval bible whose entire premise is cause->effect ('what the adjustment does and why it does it'). Verified extractable via pdftotext (clean text, 451KB). The single richest oval-family item. Also mirrored at https://www.amaintracks.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/Murfdogg_Chassis_Tuning_101.pdf

title: Buggy Setup Guide (Quick Reference)
notes: Short cheat-sheet but genuinely cause->effect ('Stiffer front: less front traction, less steering, bigger turn radius'). ~14k chars. Concise off-road primer.

title: Set-up Black Book (Danny Bartholomew)
source: Danny Bartholomew, 2001 ROAR Carpet Oval Nat'l Champ (hosted on petitrc.com)
notes: Carpet/pan-oval theory as teaching narrative — defines tweak/crossweight then explains each. ~19k chars. 'This is theory, not gospel' framing.

title: Touring Car Setting V1
notes: Touring concept notes, clear cause->effect bullets ('Lowering the roll center -> car rolls more, more overall traction, easier to drive'). ~10k chars, bullet-style. Good for roll-center/camber-link reasoning.

title: Racing Lines — On Road Setup Guide (Anthony Atack)
source: Anthony Atack / Racing Lines (hosted on petitrc.com)
notes: Multi-part on-road guide (XRAY T3 example, general principles). Each setting given lower/higher with bulleted effects. ~29k chars extract cleanly.

title: Oval Pan Car Setup Guide (2007)
notes: Confirmed valid PDF (57KB) but compressed streams need pdftotext (web-fetch markdown converter can't read it, same as HudySetupBook). Title/metadata 'Ovalsetupguide2007.doc'. Oval/pan-specific; verify exact content after pdftotext extraction.

title: Serpent 710 Setup Guide
notes: ~36-page, ~9200-word official Serpent guide split into 'Basic Setup' and 'Advanced Setup — describes the effects of setup changes.' Section B is rich cause->effect prose (front/rear roll center, on/off-throttle behavior, traction-roll). 1/10 touring; theory chassis-agnostic. Mirror host, authentic Serpent material. Highest-value touring PDF.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide (master index)
notes: Hub index linking ~50-60 individual per-setting cause->effect sub-guides; the most complete free RC concept hub found. Depth lives in the sub-pages (enumerated below). A few sub-topics (roll center) are 'Coming Soon' placeholders, and some use irregular flat slugs (/rc-tuning-differential/, /rc-tuning-shocks/) — fetch each before trusting.

title: RC Quick Setup Guide (symptom -> adjustment table)
notes: Symptom-to-fix matrix: each handling problem -> ~5-8 candidate adjustments. Generic across cars. Highest-leverage single page for a deterministic symptom->adjustment advisor; pairs with the per-parameter pages.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Camber
notes: Front/rear effect tables (more camber = less forward traction, more cornering grip, less straight-line stability), concrete ranges (-1 to -2deg front).

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Camber Link Locations
notes: Shorter vs longer links: camber gain, stability, rear stiffness/chassis roll, high-grip vs loose track guidance.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Caster
notes: Less caster = quicker steering; more = straight-line stability. Caster adds with kick-up. Concise less/more bullets.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Toe In / Toe Out
notes: Front toe-out = more turn-in / off-power steering; rear less toe-in = faster accel / more rotation. Effect-list, no mechanism.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Ride Height
notes: Lower front = less roll, more responsive; higher = more roll, better over bumps/jumps. Effect-list depth.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Droop
notes: Front/rear-segmented droop effects in cause->effect bullets (less droop -> more aggressive steering, less rear weight transfer on accel). Light on underlying mechanism.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Anti-Roll Bar (Sway Bar)
notes: Thicker bar = less chassis roll; thinner for low-traction, thicker for high-traction tracks. Basic mechanism.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Anti-Squat
notes: Rear inner hinge-pin angle; more anti-squat = more forward traction + less on-power steering + less side grip.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Kickup
notes: Front chassis angle acts as added caster (2deg kickup + 2deg caster = 4deg). Less kickup = quicker steering, less stable.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Gear Ratio
notes: Larger pinion/smaller spur = top speed, less accel, more heat; vice versa. Includes FDR formula; ties ratio to track length/temp/runtime.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Bumpsteer
notes: Defines bumpsteer, detection method, adjustment procedure, more-vs-less effects. Re-check whenever caster changes.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide – Shock Mounting Positions
notes: Tower in/out (progressive vs linear), arm in/out (soft+responsive vs stable+side grip), upright vs laid-down angle. Solid cause->effect.

title: RC Tuning Guide – Differential
notes: Tighter diff = more instant throttle response/accel; looser for low-traction, tighter for high-traction. Covers gear vs one-way. NOTE non-standard flat URL slug (/rc-tuning-differential/).

title: RC Tuning Guide – Shocks & Shock Oil
notes: Oil weight 10-100wt; lighter = responsive/bumpy + more roll, heavier = sluggish/planted/smooth tracks. Ties viscosity to piston-hole flow. NOTE non-standard flat URL slug (/rc-tuning-shocks/).

title: Suspension Tuning Guide: Part 1 – Camber & Toe-In
notes: Mechanism-level: weight transfer leans wheels -> negative camber compensates; front zero-toe vs toe-in to calm a loose car; rear toe-in for stability. Strong writing. Part 1 of 4.

title: Suspension Tuning Guide: Part 2 – Shock Absorbers
notes: Piston hole sizes (0.95-1.6mm), oil viscosity, spring rate, ride height/preload and how each changes damping force.

title: Suspension Tuning Guide: Part 3 – Shock Position & Roll Center
notes: Lever/fulcrum analogy (inboard shock = softer effective spring); lowering roll center increases CG-to-RC distance -> more roll + more cornering traction. Clear diagrams.

title: Suspension Tuning Guide: Part 4 – Sway Bars & Tuning Tips
notes: How a sway bar links arms to cut roll; stiffer = more anti-roll but less traction; link position adjusts stiffness; high- vs low-grip guidance.

title: Tamiya RC Start Guide — Car Settings (Part 2)
notes: Official Tamiya page with clean cause->effect for the full alignment + suspension set (toe-in = stability but understeer; larger caster = gentler turn-in; lower ride height = lower CG = more stability). Closest thing to an official Tamiya 'effects' guide.

title: Tamiya RC Start Guide — Car Settings (Part 1)
notes: Official Tamiya content explaining the tuning methodology + why weight/grip/balance matter. Foundational/intro.

title: Yokomo BD8 — Rear Toe Control (RTC) System
notes: Single-concept cause->effect: inboard toe (mounts) = more overall rear grip but large wheelbase change; outboard toe (knuckles) = smaller gains. Genuine but shallow.

title: Yokomo BD9 — Build and Setup Tips
notes: Mixes assembly technique with genuine cause->effect (steel screws = stiffer flex; front weights = more braking grip but mid-corner understeer; RTC = more rear traction on acceleration). Intro-to-intermediate.

title: Serpent Project 4X — Blake Ryan Setup Guide
notes: Driver-written cause->effect rationale (more negative camber generates more traction to a point, then breaks free quicker; thicker oil/fewer holes = more damping). Directional guidance with reasoning, not just numbers.

title: The M-Racing Setup Guide
notes: Single-page HTML physics reference — slip angle, circle of forces, roll-center construction, diagrams. Folder URL is canonical (guessed .htm names 404).

title: Bob Wright — The Science of Setup
source: Bob Wright / RC Crew Chief (hosted on petitrc.com)
notes: Deepest physics treatment on petitrc — weight transfer, roll stiffness, roll-center + camber gain, damping ratio, sprung/unsprung mass, engineering diagrams. Single-page HTML; folder URL is canonical.

title: Basic Suspension Tuning
notes: Single-page HTML, buggy-leaning, photos per topic, explicit cause->effect ('more toe-out makes the car smoother, increases low-speed steering by decreasing turning radius'). Folder URL is canonical.

title: THE Guide (1/8 Buggy Setup & Tuning Bible)
notes: Long-form, mechanism-level ('turbulence increases friction as piston speeds up'; 'everything affects everything'); testing+notebook methodology. Deepest free 1/8 offroad concept resource found.

title: Randy Pike's Tips for Tuning Gear Diffs
notes: Per-diff cause->effect: heavier front = slower turn-in/better on-power steering; center light = tracks straight; rear light = more rotation. 5/7/3 baseline, slippery vs high-grip, electric vs nitro.

title: Basher Basics – Shock Tuning
notes: Beginner cause->effect: too stiff = bouncing/lost traction, too soft = chassis slap/hopping. Spring vs piston roles. Basher-oriented.

title: RC Suspension Tuning Guide (Optimize Handling & Performance)
notes: Broad single-page guide with terrain-matched tables and symptom->fix correlations. Terrain-segmented sections (off-road/touring/drift/truck-SCT). Qualitative, no spring-rate numbers.

title: Basic RC Suspension Tuning: Camber, Toe, Ride Height, Springs, and Oil
notes: Clean general cause->effect explainer with a stability-vs-aggressive reference table ('preload changes ride height, not stiffness'; thinner oil for bumps, thicker for jumps; lower ride height = lower CG + less traction-rolling). Good cross-category base.

title: RC Sway Bar Tuning (Simplified)
notes: Single-topic explainer: thick vs thin bars front/rear, effect on response and rotation, low-grip/light-vehicle caveats. Deliberately simplified.

title: RC Caster Tuning (Simplified)
notes: 5 caster effects (steering response, camber gain, stability, bumps, driving style); more vs less tradeoffs. Beginner entry point.

title: RC Shock Position Tuning (Simplified)
notes: A-arm in/out and tower in/out positions; laying shock down = more progressive; front+rear recommendations + track-condition tips.

title: Setup Explained (Detailed)
notes: Solid intermediate cause->effect with diagrams; explains WHY (front toe-in = straight-line stability at cost of sluggishness), camber gain on compression, neutral-handling philosophy. On-road/F1-leaning. Does NOT cover caster/ride-height/ballast/tires.

title: RC Drift Car Ackermann Setup — How to, What and Why?
notes: Drift-specific Ackermann explainer focused on WHY it matters (inner/outer path difference, scrub reduction, leading vs trailing tire roles in drift entry/exit). Strong on concept, lighter on per-chassis steps.

title: How To Tune an RC Drift Car
notes: Broad drift tuning table pairing each adjustment with its handling effect (lowering front roll center improves corner entry; wider front = more grip vs wider rear = better exit control). Preaches one-change-at-a-time. Good breadth, moderate per-item depth.

title: RC Drift Car Setup Secrets for Australian Tracks
notes: One of the richest drift cause->effect pages. Caster 8-10deg -> stronger self-centering/countersteer but harder initiation; front 55-60% bias lets rear break predictably; gyro gain trades stability vs max angle; baseline numbers given.

title: RC Drift Gyro Setup That Actually Works
notes: Dedicated gyro deep-dive: low/moderate/high gain behaviors, rate vs heading-hold modes, countersteer direction-check test, why fast servo matters. Strong on gain-tuning methodology; lighter on gyro physics.

title: RE-Xtreme Drift Bible — RWD Drift Setup
notes: RWD-drift-specific cause->effect ('toe in = forced understeer = scrubbing speed'; anti-squat via spacers; vertical vs horizontal weight from battery placement). Field-tested settings over geometry math. No caster/ackermann/droop.

title: RC Drift Chassis & Suspension Setup Guide for Beginners
notes: Beginner drift orientation. Touches camber/toe/weight-bias/steering-angle but mostly single-sentence statements without deep cause->effect chains. Intro-tier source only.

title: Simple RC Drift Car Guide
notes: Beginner overview of the drift setup surface area. Prescriptive ('softer front/stiffer rear helps initiate drift') without the why. Intro tier; pairs with the deeper Hearns 'Secrets' page.

title: Crawler Setup — Key Elements
notes: Crawler-specific priorities with cause->effect: lower CG improves climb/descend/sidehill; 60/40 front bias aids climbing; stiffer springs resist torque-twist on sidehills. No link-geometry/droop numbers. Solid crawler conceptual primer.

title: Crawler theory — Weight (forum thread)
notes: Community theory thread, genuinely instructional on weight: 60-62% front improves climb but worsens descent; ballast on knuckles/axles adds unsprung-low weight without rotating-mass penalty. Multi-post forum format, RC-specific.

title: What Are Droop & Downstop on an RC Car? Setup & Tuning Guide
notes: Droop vs downstop distinction, front/rear effects, three measurement methods. Applies across pan/oval/crawler. Good practical cause->effect; light on geometry. (So Dialed is RaceLab's direct competitor — useful concept benchmark.)

title: What Is Wedge on an RC Car? Setup & Tuning Guide
notes: Defines wedge/cross-weight (RF+LR vs LF+RR) with the formula and the two key effects: more wedge = more push/less steering but drives out of turns better. Glossary-tier intro stated correctly.

title: What Is Ackermann on an RC Car? Setup & Tuning Guide
notes: Ackermann defined as toe-angle change through steering travel; more positive = smoother/more off-power control, less = twitchier on-power steering. Glossary-tier; applies to F1/pan/oval/drift.

title: RC Oval Camber Link & Roll Center Cheatsheet
notes: RC-oval-specific quick-reference: which camber-link/roll-center moves add vs reduce grip. Directional 'do this to get that' without mechanism. Useful as an oval-specific lookup.

title: Dirt Oval RC Setup Troubleshooting — Loose, Push & Traction
notes: Symptom->fix dirt-oval troubleshooter (softer RF spring -> more steering/less push), impact-ranked lists. Cause->effect at the symptom level. Pairs with the Murfdogg PDF for the oval family.

title: Setup Explained (RC F1 Setup Guide)
notes: F1-specific 'setup explained' page built around cause->effect chains (softer springs -> more roll -> more weight transfer). Alternate URL path to the same/related RC Formula1 content. Does NOT cover caster/ride-height/ballast/tires on this page.

title: Mark Payne's 1/12th Scale RC Notes
notes: 1/12-pan-specific build/setup blog: precise ride-height (0.2mm L/R), eliminating front droop via spring shimming, soft front springs (0.018), L/R caster checking, tweak as ongoing concern. Emphasis on mechanical execution over the 'why'.
